relevance_note: Single-family case report of a girl and relatives carrying a TNFAIP3 variant: "We identified a heterozygous variant in TNFAIP3, namely NM_006290.4:c.460G > T" and "The same TNFAIP3 variant was also found in her father".
method_note: Built with a short Python script from my own reading; spans matched to the paper text (the paper uses thin spaces around '>' in the variant). No tables in the paper. Labels: proband 'patient' (rule 5); relatives by rule 2 relative to the proband, using the paper's wording ('her father', 'the baby girl's mother', 'her father's brother', 'a paternal grandfather', 'brother of paternal grandfather', 'father's uncle'). 'brother of paternal grandfather' and 'father's uncle' are listed separately in the family history and kept as two people, although they could be the same person; the paper does not say. Mother is in scope as a tested relative (screened for TNFAIP3); the paper only implies she is negative via 'paternal origin', so no variant row. The maternally inherited TNFRSF13B allele (patient and mother) is called a 'known risk allele' and was not recorded as a variant row (risk alleles excluded). Father and father's brother variant rows: the paper says they carry 'the same' variant; zygosity and inheritance not stated for them, left not reported. Variant type 'nonsense' taken from 'resulting in a premature stop codon' for this exact variant. Pathogenicity left not reported: the authors call it 'novel' / 'not previously described' but give no classification. Age at last evaluation not reported: 'one-year-old' is age at first presentation, follow-up continued afterwards. n_patients_reported left null: no count stated (three carriers described). Not recorded as features: steroid 'side effects (weight gain, changes in mood and behaviour, diabetes.)' because it is unclear whether these are the patient's own; ADA-2 deficiency and VEO-IBD genetic exclusions (diagnoses, not features); normal vital signs and normal cardiovascular/thoracic/abdominal examination at the ER visit (whole examinations, exclude nothing specific); later negative inflammatory markers after treatment (resolution, not absence). Checklist: 'recurrent fever' not reported (one febrile episode described, not recurrence); 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' not reported (ASCA and ANCA normal but ANA not mentioned; narrow does not exclude broad); 'lymphoproliferation' not reported (colonic lymphoid nodular hyperplasia only 'suggestive'); 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' not reported (anemia attributed to GI bleeding); father's 'autoimmune thyroiditis' marked observed because the paper lists his thyroiditis under 'autoimmune conditions'. No contradictions found in the paper.
